key_insight: AI-derived ECG features outperformed 15 morphology measurements for 30-day mortality prediction, but added little discrimination beyond expanded automated ECG reports plus basic clinical history.
clinical_relevance: Similar predictive performance can mask substantially different patient review lists, making patient selection an important consideration alongside overall accuracy.
method: Compared AI-derived waveform features with 15 prespecified ECG morphology measurements using identical prediction procedures.
Held basic clinical history constant in selected comparisons and reported paired 95% confidence intervals.
Examined hypothetical 5% review-capacity lists; expanded-report comparisons were post hoc.
evidence_signal: Among 25,430 held-out MIMIC-IV patients with 924 deaths, AI versus morphology achieved AUROC 0.812 versus 0.737; adding AI to reports plus history improved AUROC by 0.0075, with a 95% CI spanning zero.
watch_item: Hypothetical review-list analyses do not establish clinical benefit: separately refitted AI and report models captured similar death totals but shared only 654 of 1,272 flagged patients.
paper_title: Evaluating the Incremental Value of AI-Derived ECG Features Beyond Automated ECG Reports and Clinical Data for 30-Day Mortality: A MIMIC-IV Cohort Study
